synopsis: The corpus treats model credibility as a separate task requiring comparison with reality, independent validation evidence, and distinct calibration, validation and withheld-confirmation datasets; failed validation cases must remain recorded [f11310, f12123, f7589, f7590]. Physical tests anchor the validated domain, simulation fills its interior, and physical confirmation remains necessary at boundaries and after influential changes; existing warning-system history cannot validate the new closed-loop braking chain [f7536, f7575]. Important evidence gaps persist: no published validation of heavy-machine braking distance on gravel, mud, ice or slopes was found, sensor studies mostly address individual effects on road vehicles or in laboratories, and the organization currently lacks the described simulation-credibility foundations [f253, f4408, f10414]. A program starting in October 2026 could realistically achieve SIL with partly validated sensor models by mid-2027, but sensor calibration requires real sensors; the final four-month campaign is variously framed as confirmation plus calibration, calibration and testing, or confirmation rather than tuning [f65, f914, f70, f3772, f1611]. The recommended stopping-distance core is a calibrated point-mass model with measured latency, brake build-up lag and condition-dependent worst-case deceleration, while machine-class VIL or proving-ground stops should validate the brake model; the 2025 AGX wheel-loader example demonstrates calibration against a physical machine, not a stated independent-validation result [f5905, f5558, f8292].
